question: What does the term utterance include here, and why does that distinguish the Shakta means?
premises: The word utterance here includes outward-directed operations and related forms.
These do not define the Shakta means in the same way.
The Shakta means is characterized by difference and nondifference, which is the nature of power.
inference: Therefore utterance and similar outer operations are not the defining mark of the Shakta means, because that means is constituted by the power-play of difference and nondifference.
uncertainties: bahvantena is terse; the exact range of included operations is inferred from context.
plain_english: Here the word utterance covers outward expression and related operations. These are not what define the Shakta means, because the Shakta means is characterized by the play of difference and nondifference, which is the very nature of power.
